solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leaped — above oneself?

definitions.meaning: sprang upwards, rose with a bound
conceited, giving oneself airs above one's station

explanation.surface: A leap seems to lift someone above themselves, a playful question about pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal past tense of springing upward and an idiom for an upstart who behaves with undue self-importance.

clue.text: International group is performing in concert

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, a group of nations
an actor who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: A multinational ensemble is giving a live show together.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means together in agreement, which is the idiomatic sense of doing something together as one voice.

clue.text: Floral decoration in plate manufacture

indicators.note: manufacture means making something, so these letters are put together afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A flower pattern painted onto a dinner plate during production.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaf of a bloom is part of its natural adornment, so a floral decoration is a fair description.

clue.text: Party dress container found in good order

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a mini is a short dress
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: Party clothes and a box are discovered neatly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican friar belongs to a religious order, punningly a 'good order' of holy men, rather than tidiness.

clue.text: Reading 'Country Girl'

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: Someone is reading a book titled 'Country Girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful read through a text is a perusal, the noun for examining written matter.

clue.text: Cut it and keep quiet

parts.note: the idiom 'cut the ...' means stop the idle chatter, and 'it' stands for the noisy chatter itself

explanation.surface: An order to stop doing something and fall silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'cut the cackle' is a British idiom meaning stop chattering and get to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy chatter is what one is told to cut in the familiar idiom urging silence.

clue.text: Beg for keys

parts.note: C is the name of a musical key
A is the name of a musical key
D is the name of a musical key
G is the name of a musical key
E is the name of a musical key

explanation.surface: Asking for someone's keys, perhaps to borrow a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' supplies five letters at once, each one a musical key; 'for' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge or ask for something without intending to pay is a synonym of begging.

clue.text: They spend their time together

parts.note: the 'time' is a prison sentence, and these people share a room while serving it

explanation.surface: A description of close companions who are always together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' here means a prison term, as in doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners sharing a single cell serve their sentences side by side.

clue.text: It's not a close-up, you can bet on it

definitions.meaning: a camera shot taken from a distance, the opposite of a close-up
an outsider with poor odds that gamblers may back

explanation.surface: A film shot that is distant yet tempting to a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a film term for a distant shot and a betting term for an unlikely runner.

clue.text: Two men cut down prey

parts.note: Vic is a shortened form of the man's name Victor
Tim is a shortened form of the man's name Timothy

explanation.surface: Two hunters fell an animal they were stalking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' points to the names being clipped forms, Vic and Tim.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who falls to an attacker is their prey, an equivalent noun.

clue.text: Evocative of European river ebbing fast

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the river's name runs backwards

parts.note: the Oder is a river in central Europe
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A description of a fast-flowing river in Europe going out with the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent of or smelling of a thing is said to be suggestive of it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Knots of painters?

parts.note: a painter is a rope at the front of a small boat, so its knots are those tied in ropes at the bow

explanation.surface: Seemingly a question about groups of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painters' are not artists but ropes used to tie up a boat at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: These are common sailors' knots and also, read in two parts, ropes at a boat's prow.

clue.text: She and men get involved and become engaged

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman and some men become romantically entangled and get engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught up or entangled in something, as in a net, is to become engaged with it.

clue.text: Speed check

parts.note: a reduction or slowing of velocity, not a radar test

explanation.surface: A police radar inspection of motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowing down is literally a curb on velocity, the technical term for reducing speed.

clue.text: Funny comedian touring North, in total control

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shuffled letters go around another
funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters come out strange and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hilarious comic travelling around the north of England dominates his audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges COMEDIAN as DOMIANCE; 'touring' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in total control means having supremacy or power over others, a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Make a series of calls on zero zero

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the figure zero
a round figure is the shape of a zero

explanation.surface: Phoning a number made of two zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephoning several people one after another is a British phrasal verb for phoning around.

clue.text: Agree to get less

definitions.meaning: to agree terms formally, signing a deal

explanation.surface: Accepting a deal that leaves one worse off.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to enter a binding deal and to shrink in size.

clue.text: Holy orders?

parts.note: not ordination, but sacred instructions, such as the ten given to Moses

explanation.surface: An allusion to ordination into the priesthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy orders' usually means ordination; here it means divine instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten given on Sinai are sacred instructions, literally orders from God.

clue.text: It will give you warmth and peace

definitions.meaning: a scarf worn round the neck to keep warm
a device such as a car silencer that brings quiet

explanation.surface: Something that offers both comfort and tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: A car silencer is called this in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a warm scarf and a noise-deadening device that provides quiet.

clue.text: Uncover swindle

definitions.meaning: to strip a sheep of its woolly coat
to cheat someone out of money

explanation.surface: Exposing a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to shear wool from a sheep and to rob someone by trickery.

clue.text: Doesn't fancy being under the influence

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes being intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges DOESNT; 'Doesn't fancy' reads as dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Being high on drugs or drink is slang for being intoxicated.

clue.text: Financial obligation limits university entrance

indicators.note: limits means borders or encloses, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a debt is money owed

explanation.surface: Student loans restrict who can go to university.
explanation.definitionFit: A first public appearance is someone's entry onto the stage or scene.

clue.text: Anticipate warning shout to Gessler's opponent

parts.note: 'fore' is the warning shout in golf
William Tell defied the tyrant Gessler in the Swiss legend

explanation.surface: Calling a warning to the Swiss hero's enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend, Gessler forced William Tell to shoot an apple off his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict something is to anticipate it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Discrimination 23 Across appreciates in people

definitions.meaning: a fine sense of judgement in matters of style
the flavour a man-eater enjoys in humans

explanation.surface: A dark joke about a man-eater's preferences in humans.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 Across is CANNIBAL, who enjoys people's flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means aesthetic judgement and also the flavour of food.

clue.text: One gets fed up with people

definitions.text: One gets fed up with people

parts.words: One gets fed up with people
parts.note: 'fed up' reads not as weary but as having eaten humans

explanation.surface: Someone tired of other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is literally full after a meal of humans.

clue.text: Result in changes for part of Ireland

indicators.note: letters put through changes are altered and reshuffled

explanation.surface: An election outcome brings change to a region of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in changes' rearranges RESULT. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the four historic provinces of the island, in its north.

clue.text: Many dwell on this anagram made by setter

indicators.note: the clue openly says the letters are rearranged from the next word

explanation.surface: A setter jokes about making an anagram for where people live.
explanation.definitionFit: Many people live on a road lined with houses, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Bought back, having had second thoughts?

explanation.surface: Something repurchased after reconsideration.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means repurchased and, split playfully, considered once more.
